page.layout: One column of running text on a single printed page; headings centred above their entries; a catchword-free page with the running head at top and page number at top left; a small note "In vi-" at lower right of the text block, no marginal notes.

main_text.head: VENIÆ: Vide supra Tit. EXCUSATIONIS.
main_text.p: AB ætate sæpè veniam impetramus culpæ. Mere 5. 4. v. 37.
main_text.head: VERITATIS.
main_text.p: VERITAS vi interdum extorquetur. Truc. 4. 3. v. 9.
main_text.head: VERMIUM. LUMBRICORUM.
main_text.p: LUMBICI è terrâ erépunt. Aul. 4. 4. v. 1. Foràs lumbrice, quì sub terrâ crepsti modò, qui modò nunquam comparebas: nunc cum compares, perit. Ita Græcis dicuntur ἔντερα γῆς.
main_text.head: VICISSITUDINIS-RERUM.
main_text.p: VICISSITUDO rerum humanarum est, ut quod quis habet, paulò post alius possideat. Truc. 2. 1, v. 8. De bonis amato-rum. Vide etiam Tit. Fortunæ.
main_text.head: VICTORIÆ. TRIUMPHI.
main_text.p: VIRTUTIS vera est victoria. Cist. 1. 3. v. 46. Ea parit laudem & lauream.

page.notes: Initial letters A, V, L, V are large woodcut initials; the marginal ornament at lower right is a decorative mark. Greek phrase ἔντερα γῆς read from scan, doubtful.
